document.abstract: Television systems with 1000 line or greater resolution have been available for several decades, but the relatively wide transmission bandwidths required have limited useage to short distances. The availability of satellite transponders, particularly DBS services, and the resulting greater amount of available spectrum space has stimulated renewed activity in this field, especially in high quality color video for the entertainment field.

authors.bio: Glen R. Southworth claims a certain amount of literate and inventive ability, being the author of over one hundred papers and having been issued six patents. Born in Moscow, Idaho, he owes much to the University of Idaho, Washington State University, and the Southeastern Signal School, all of whom, inretrospect, seemed remarkably tolerant and friendly. Southworth's television career began in 1953 as “Director of Television Studios” at Washington State University. He joined the staff of Ball Brothers Research Corporation in 1960, spending four years in the development of high resolution digital TV systems, and in 1965 founded Colorado Video, where he remains to this day.
